stubs.angle: Given three middleware registered with app.Use that each log before and after calling next, which order of log lines does one request produce?
stubs.answerHinge: Middleware run in registration order on the way in and in reverse order on the way out, because each one wraps the rest of the pipeline.

stubs.angle: Select the true statements about app.Use, app.Run and app.Map when building the request pipeline.
stubs.answerHinge: app.Run registers terminal middleware that never calls a next delegate, app.Use can call or skip next, and app.Map branches the pipeline by request path.

stubs.angle: Explain the Transient, Scoped and Singleton lifetimes in the ASP.NET Core container and give a typical service for each.
stubs.answerHinge: Transient creates an instance per resolution, Scoped creates one per scope, which in ASP.NET Core is one per HTTP request, and Singleton creates one for the whole application lifetime.

stubs.angle: Which environment variable name overrides the configuration key Logging:LogLevel:Default on every platform?
stubs.answerHinge: The environment variables provider maps a double underscore __ to the colon separator, so the variable is Logging__LogLevel__Default.

stubs.angle: What is a minimal API endpoint, how does it differ from a controller action, and what does each approach look like in Program.cs?
stubs.answerHinge: Minimal APIs map a route directly to a delegate with MapGet and similar methods, while controllers group actions in classes discovered by MVC with attribute routing, model binding conventions and MVC filters.

stubs.angle: Select the true statements about how ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT affects an ASP.NET Core application.
stubs.answerHinge: When no environment is set the app runs as Production, and the environment name selects appsettings.{Environment}.json, which is loaded after appsettings.json and overrides it.

stubs.angle: Find the line where a service registered as Singleton takes a scoped DbContext through its constructor and keeps it for the app lifetime.
stubs.answerHinge: A singleton that depends on a scoped service captures one instance forever (a captive dependency); scope validation in Development throws at resolution, and the fix is a scoped registration or IServiceScopeFactory.

stubs.angle: Find the line in a custom middleware that adds a response header after await next() when the endpoint has already written the body.
stubs.answerHinge: Once the response has started, headers are sent and modifying them throws InvalidOperationException; headers must be set before next or in Response.OnStarting.

stubs.angle: A singleton service must see new values after appsettings.json changes at runtime; which options interface should it inject?
stubs.answerHinge: IOptions<T> is computed once and IOptionsSnapshot<T> is scoped so it cannot be injected into a singleton; only IOptionsMonitor<T> is a singleton that returns reloaded values and raises change notifications.

stubs.angle: An interface is registered twice with AddSingleton and two implementations; which instance does a constructor that asks for the interface receive?
stubs.answerHinge: Resolving a single service returns the last registration, while IEnumerable<T> returns all registrations in order; TryAdd would have skipped the second one.

stubs.angle: When does an MVC exception filter catch an exception and when do you need exception handling middleware instead?
stubs.answerHinge: Exception filters only see exceptions thrown inside the MVC action invocation (actions, model binding, other filters), while UseExceptionHandler placed early catches exceptions from any later middleware, routing and minimal API endpoints.

stubs.angle: An action has no ModelState.IsValid check yet invalid input never reaches it; which feature explains this behaviour?
stubs.answerHinge: The [ApiController] attribute adds a filter that returns an automatic HTTP 400 with ValidationProblemDetails when model state is invalid, before the action runs.

stubs.angle: Select the true statements about applying filter logic to minimal API endpoints.
stubs.answerHinge: MVC action filters run only inside the MVC action invoker and do not apply to minimal APIs; minimal APIs use IEndpointFilter added with AddEndpointFilter, available since .NET 7.

stubs.angle: Select the registrations that make an application with an invalid required options section fail at startup instead of on the first request that uses it.
stubs.answerHinge: Options validation runs lazily on first access of Value unless ValidateOnStart is added, so fail-fast needs validation rules such as ValidateDataAnnotations together with ValidateOnStart.

stubs.angle: List the default configuration sources of WebApplication.CreateBuilder in the order they are added and explain which value wins when a key appears in several.
stubs.answerHinge: Sources are added as appsettings.json, appsettings.{Environment}.json, user secrets in Development, environment variables, then command-line arguments, and the last provider that sets a key wins.

stubs.subtopic: DI scopes and the request lifetime
stubs.angle: Find the line where a controller starts a fire-and-forget Task.Run that uses the injected DbContext after the action has returned.
stubs.answerHinge: The request scope and its scoped services are disposed when the request ends, so background work must create its own scope with IServiceScopeFactory instead of capturing request services.

stubs.angle: Why does memory grow when a transient IDisposable service is resolved repeatedly from the root IServiceProvider, and how do you fix it?
stubs.answerHinge: The container tracks disposable transients for disposal when their scope ends, and the root scope ends only at application shutdown, so each resolution stays referenced; resolve inside a created scope or use a factory the caller disposes.

stubs.angle: What happens to hosted services and in-flight work when the host receives SIGTERM, and what limits how long they get to finish?
stubs.answerHinge: The host signals stopping and calls StopAsync on hosted services in reverse order, cancelling the stopping token, and waits at most HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout (30 seconds by default since .NET 6) before ending the process.

stubs.angle: After moving the app behind a TLS-terminating load balancer, generated links use http and logs show the balancer address as every client IP; what do you do?
stubs.answerHinge: Kestrel only sees the proxy connection, so the app must use the Forwarded Headers middleware early in the pipeline with KnownProxies or KnownNetworks configured to trust X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For.

stubs.angle: On .NET 8 an app never logs that it is listening after a BackgroundService was added whose ExecuteAsync starts with a synchronous polling loop; how do you diagnose and fix it?
stubs.answerHinge: Before .NET 10, BackgroundService.StartAsync runs ExecuteAsync synchronously until its first await, so synchronous work blocks host startup; yield early, move the loop to async code, or rely on .NET 10 where ExecuteAsync runs entirely as a background task.

stubs.angle: Half of your team wants new endpoints in minimal APIs while an existing service has 150 controller actions with MVC filters; how do you decide and roll out the choice?
stubs.answerHinge: The decision rests on which controller features the service depends on (MVC filters, conventions, model binding behaviour) and on consistency cost: mixing both in one service is supported but cross-cutting logic must be duplicated as endpoint filters, so set an explicit rule per service and migrate only with a reason.

stubs.angle: How would you design configuration management for 40 ASP.NET Core services so that settings can change at runtime without redeploys, and what risks does it bring?
stubs.answerHinge: Add a central store as another IConfiguration provider with local values as fallback, have code read IOptionsMonitor for reloadable settings, and treat runtime changes as deployments: versioned, validated, audited and rolled out gradually because a bad value now reaches every service at once.
